basis: Breast is outside the organ axes; mastitis includes sterile obstructive inflammation, so infection or autoimmunity is not defining.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: this umbrella includes noninfectious obstructive inflammation; inflammation alone does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated disease.

basis: Spastic paraplegia, neuropathy and defining optic involvement; persistent distal amyotrophy and pes cavus occur in 30-79%, supporting musculoskeletal damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: distal amyotrophy and structural pes cavus each occur in 30-79%; persistent tissue wasting and deformity qualify despite their neurogenic origin.

basis: Multisite tuberculosis; pulmonary infection accompanies roughly half of cases, exceeding 30%. Other organ sites vary.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary infection accompanies approximately 50% of multifocal tuberculosis over its course; lung involvement is common but not required.

basis: Axonal sensorimotor neuropathy; sustained distal muscle wasting in 20/20 patients constitutes common muscle tissue loss, even though caused by denervation.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: distal amyotrophy in 20/20 patients is persistent muscle tissue loss caused by the neuropathy; a primary myopathy is not required for this tier.

basis: SCID with defining profound T-lymphocyte deficiency affects immune function and blood cells; secondary infections are separate diseases.

decisions.haematologic: primary: the T-B+ phenotype is defined by absent or profoundly reduced T lymphocytes, a blood-cell deficiency, alongside combined immunodeficiency.

basis: Blood dyscrasia, telangiectasias and hypoxemic pulmonary shunts define TEMPI; CNS hemorrhage 30-79%. Perinephric fluid need not damage kidneys; autoimmunity unproven.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: defining telangiectasias (100%) are vascular lesions; pulmonary vascular abnormalities occur in 80-99%, and venous thrombosis in 30-79%.
decisions.pulmonary: primary: intrapulmonary shunting is a defining manifestation with hypoxemia in 100%; pulmonary vascular abnormalities and pleural effusions occur in 80-99%.
decisions.renal: none: perinephric collections, despite the broad kidney HPO annotation, do not establish kidney tissue damage or impaired renal function.
decisions.infectious_immune: none: TEMPI is a plasma-cell dyscrasia-associated syndrome; an autoimmune parent alone does not establish a proven autoimmune or other qualifying immune mechanism.

basis: UV-related skin disease; neurodegeneration affects >50% in XPA, chronic ocular surface damage >50%, and sensorineural hearing loss approximately 30-50% over the course.

decisions.otologic: involved: progressive sensorineural hearing loss is a common component of XPA neurodegeneration, affecting approximately 30-50% over the typical course.

basis: Raised intracranial pressure and diagnostic optic-disc edema define IIH. Papilledema is a major criterion; visual loss occurs in 5-29%.

decisions.ocular: primary: sustained papilledema is optic-nerve involvement and a major diagnostic criterion; the 5-29% frequency of visual loss does not negate this defining feature.

basis: Acute inflammation of orbital tissues; the umbrella does not establish infection or an immune-mediated mechanism across most cases.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: infectious children establish possible etiologies, not a required or predominant mechanism for this broad orbital inflammation concept.

basis: Primary neuronal channelopathy with peripheral neuropathy in 80-99%; episodic redness and vasomotor changes do not establish lasting skin or vessel injury.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: episodic acral vasodilation is not established vessel injury; vasculitis is only occasional (5-29%), not defining.
